claim: HMN initialization gives adjacent coordinates 0.52 cosine similarity and helps learning (GPL Tokenizer, /Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer)
evidence: The 0.52 figure is real and reproducible: re-running the measurement from tests/test_embedding.py (Suite 4: 196 level-4 horizontally adjacent pairs at d_model=128) gives HMN mean cosine 0.5213 vs random init 0.0050, matching the docstring derivation in embedding/hmn_init.py (sinusoidal cell-center encoding, freq 1–64, plus shared level marker and noise). Caveats: (1) it is config-dependent — the README/RESEARCH_SUMMARY value comes from the d=128 test config, while the production model uses d_model=256 where the value is 0.5003 (hmn_init.py itself admits 0.52 is a design artifact, not a target); (2) much of the 0.52 is not spatial proximity but shared level marker/norm: far pairs sit at 0.45–0.49, so adjacent-minus-far gap is only ~0.05, and decay is non-monotonic (dist=4 sim 0.452 < dist=8 sim 0.487) due to aliasing of the period-1 frequencies in _spatial_encoding — contradicting the docstring claim that similarity "decreases smoothly with adjacency"; (3) "helps learning" has no experiment anywhere in the repo. The only training result (RESEARCH_SUMMARY line 77: 200 synthetic samples, 10 epochs, loss 7.81→2.91) is a single run with use_hmn_init=True; no run with use_hmn_init=False exists, so the learning claim is asserted from theory only. This matters because the literature is split: HiVG (2026) supports ordering-aware init helping, but FoNE/CNM show alternatives where init isn't the lever, and the briefing's correct skepticism applies — self-defined metrics on tiny synthetic data are weak evidence.
fix: (1) Run the existing trainer (training/trainer.py) as a 2x init ablation — use_hmn_init True vs False, identical 200-sample dataset, 10+ epochs, ≥3 seeds — and report loss curves, token accuracy, and valid-SVG rate to convert "helps learning" into a measured ~X% claim or drop it. (2) Restate the README to "≈0.50–0.52 depending on d_model" and report adjacent-minus-far cosine (~0.05) as the actual spatial bias, not 0.52 alone. (3) Fix the encoding aliasing so similarity decays monotonically (start freqs below 1.0 or use RBF/Fourier init à la HiVG/FoNE), then re-measure.

claim: GPL Tokenizer round-trip is lossless / fidelity within (cell_size/2)*sqrt(2)
evidence: The claim conflates two statements with very different support. (1) The analytic bound is correct and verified: /Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer/tokenizer/arcs.py:217-225 dequantizes to the cell center, so the max L2 error is the half-diagonal (cell_size/2)*sqrt(2), implemented at arcs.py:252-266. I re-ran /Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer/tests/test_fidelity.py (17/17 pass): 1000 random points give max error 51.87 <= bound 53.03 at the default coarsest level 2, and a corner point hits the bound exactly (53.0330, passing only via the 1e-6 float tolerance at arcs.py:309). (2) "Lossless" is false and contradicted by the project's own numbers: README.md:64 reports ~49 px max coordinate error at default settings (min_level=2 on a 300 px canvas, i.e. 16% of canvas width) improving to ~2.6 px with adaptive refinement. RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:53 claims "Lossless SVG -> GPL -> SVG round-trip verified across 47 test cases", but the test that supposedly verifies it (/Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer/tests/test_roundtrip.py:295) asserts only `len(result.token_ids) > 2 and len(recovered_d) > 0` — i.e. the detokenized string is non-empty. No command-sequence equality, no coordinate comparison, no render comparison anywhere in the suite. Additional caveats: (a) the bound only holds for in-canvas coordinates — quantize() clamps input to [0, canvas) but roundtrip_fidelity computes error against the unclamped original, so out-of-range input silently violates the bound; (b) the empirical check is circular (the quantizer is tested against its own bound on synthetic points — internal consistency, not fidelity evidence); (c) the headline 49->2.6 px "19x improvement" comes from a 4-point sample (test_fidelity.py:93). Versus literature: the bound itself is standard, uncontroversial quantization math, but no peer (IconShop, OmniSVG, HiVG, StarVector) calls quantized coordinates "lossless", and the field measures fidelity with render-based SSIM/LPIPS/FID (HiVG: SSIM 0.896/LPIPS 0.114), which GPL never computes. GPL's default level-2 grid (4x4 cells, 53 px bound) and even its finest level-6 grid (64x64) are far coarser than the de facto 200x200 standard (OmniSVG), whose equivalent bound is ~0.7 px.
fix: Three concrete changes to make the claim defensible: (1) Reword: drop "lossless" everywhere (RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:53, README.md:57 "perfectly"); state "structure-preserving round-trip with coordinate quantization error analytically bounded by (cell_size/2)*sqrt(2) at the coarsest leaf level — 3.31 px at level 6, 53 px at the default min_level=2, on a 300 px canvas". (2) Strengthen test_roundtrip.py:295: re-parse the recovered d-string with PathParser and assert (a) command-type sequence equality with the original and (b) per-coordinate L2 error <= ARCS.theoretical_max_error(coarsest observed level); also fix the out-of-canvas hole by measuring error against the clamped coordinate or asserting inputs are in-range. (3) Add the field-standard experiment: rasterize original vs reconstructed SVGs (e.g. cairosvg/resvg at 512px) over a real icon set (FIGR-8 or an SVG-Stack sample, not the 7 hand-written test SVGs) and report SSIM/LPIPS alongside the coordinate bound — this is what HiVG/OmniSVG/StarVector report and is the only way the fidelity claim is comparable to published baselines. Optionally raise the default min_level (2 -> 4+) since a 53 px worst case on a 300 px canvas makes the default configuration visibly lossy.

claim: The cited foundations exist: HiVG hierarchical SVG tokenization, StrokeNUWA, LLM4SVG, VectorGym (Rodriguez et al.)
evidence: All four works cited in README.md:93-98 and RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:128-135 of /Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer are real, with correct author attributions and accurate one-line descriptions. (1) HiVG (Xing et al.) = "Hierarchical SVG Tokenization: Learning Compact Visual Programs for SVG Modeling," arXiv:2604.05072 (Apr 2026), first author Xing; its atomic+segment two-level scheme matches both the repo's description and the literature context (2,450 atomic + 500 segment tokens, ~2.7x compression). (2) StrokeNUWA (Tang et al.) = ICML 2024, Zecheng Tang et al., VQ stroke tokens — matches literature context. (3) LLM4SVG (Xing et al.) = "Empowering LLMs to Understand and Generate Complex Vector Graphics," CVPR 2025, arXiv:2412.11102, Ximing Xing first author — the README gloss tracks the real title. (4) VectorGym (Rodriguez et al.) = "VectorGym: A Multitask Benchmark for SVG Code Generation, Sketching, and Editing," arXiv:2603.29852 (Feb 2026), first author Juan Rodriguez (ServiceNow/StarVector group), dataset at huggingface.co/datasets/ServiceNow/VectorGym — initially the most suspect citation since it is absent from the provided literature context, but it checks out (it postdates that context's benchmark list). The citations are also load-bearing in code: tokenizer/primitive_tokenizer.py explicitly positions its primitive tokens against HiVG's segment tokens, and embedding/hmn_init.py implements an HiVG-HMN-style geometry-aware embedding initialization.
fix: No fix needed for the existence claim itself. Two hardening steps: (1) soften README.md line 93 "Built on peer-reviewed research" to "Built on recent research" or split the list — StrokeNUWA (ICML 2024) and LLM4SVG (CVPR 2025) are peer-reviewed, but HiVG (arXiv:2604.05072) and VectorGym (arXiv:2603.29852, under OpenReview review) are 2026 preprints; (2) add full citations (titles, venues/arXiv IDs, links) to the four bullets in README.md and RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md so the references are independently checkable — currently only surname-style attributions are given, and HiVG's name collides with an unrelated 2024 visual-grounding paper (HiVG, Xiao et al.), which the arXiv ID would disambiguate.
